The dialogue presents a clinical scenario of a restrained driver involved in a rear-end motor vehicle collision, now presenting with acute bilateral knee pain and severe right groin pain since the accident. - Lumbar spine X-ray to exclude radicular causes of groin pain;

A restrained driver sustained a rear-end motor vehicle collision and immediately developed severe right groin pain and bilateral knee pain. 2. **Rule out associated injuries**:

3. **Exclude mimics/comorbidities**:  
   - Septic arthritis or hemarthrosis (joint aspiration if effusion present)  
   - Lumbar radiculopathy (lumbar X-ray — though MRI would be more sensitive if suspicion remains)

**Urgency:** Posterior hip dislocation is an orthopedic emergency. Untreated, it risks avascular necrosis of the femoral head, nerve injury, and post-traumatic arthritis. Time-to-reduction <6 hours significantly improves outcomes.
